bw: Slept in contact lens, foreign body sensation
Pain after lens removal, normal acuity
w: Ocular ultrasonography evaluates posterior segment pathology or foreign bodies, not corneal surface defects.
Gonioscopy views the anterior chamber angle for glaucoma.
p: Corneal abrasion is diagnosed with fluorescein under cobalt-blue light; treat with topical antibiotics (cover Pseudomonas in lens wearers) and avoid patching.

w: Balloon tamponade is for variceal bleeding.
Observation alone would not correct uremic bleeding and volume overload.
p: Uremia impairs platelet function; dialysis improves bleeding, and desmopressin can help.

x: mandatory laparotomy versus CT for abdominal gunshot wounds debated

w: Alzheimer disease progresses over years without early myoclonus.
Normal pressure hydrocephalus causes gait disturbance and incontinence, and responds to shunting.
p: CJD (prion): rapid dementia, myoclonus, 14-3-3 protein in CSF and periodic sharp waves on EEG; spongiform change on pathology.

bw: Watery diarrhea and fever after IV antibiotics
w: Intravenous vancomycin does not reach the colonic lumen.
Ciprofloxacin is a predisposing antibiotic and not therapy for C. difficile.
p: C. difficile infection is treated with oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin; stop the offending antibiotic.

w: A chest tube is for large or symptomatic primary pneumothorax.
Needle decompression is for tension pneumothorax with hemodynamic compromise.
p: Small, stable primary spontaneous pneumothorax is observed with oxygen and a follow-up film; advise smoking cessation.

bw: Non-pitting leg swelling after travel to Kenya
Thick rough indurated skin, low fever
w: Raised venous pressure causes pitting edema with varicosities and hemosiderin skin changes.
DVT presents with acute pain and swelling, not chronic non-pitting edema.
p: Lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti) obstructs lymphatics causing non-pitting elephantiasis; treat with diethylcarbamazine.

w: Open commissurotomy is for refractory symptoms or severe stenosis.
Valve replacement is not first line for medically controllable pregnancy symptoms.
p: Mitral stenosis worsens in pregnancy with volume load and tachycardia; treat with diuretics and beta-blockers, intervention only if refractory.

bw: New painkiller, then tremor, vomiting, hyperreflexia
w: Atorvastatin does not affect lithium clearance.
Metoprolol does not raise lithium levels.
p: NSAIDs, thiazides and ACE inhibitors reduce renal lithium excretion and cause toxicity (tremor, vomiting, confusion).

w: Cesarean adds maternal morbidity and is avoided in intrauterine fetal demise.
Dilation and curettage is for early pregnancy loss before the second trimester.
p: Intrauterine fetal demise at 24-26 weeks is managed with induction of labor (misoprostol or oxytocin) for vaginal delivery.

x: Charcot arthropathy vs tertiary syphilis ambiguous

bw: Perioral numbness after massive blood loss
w: Hypoparathyroidism is possible but this acute onset follows transfusion citrate binding calcium.
Peripheral nerve injury would not produce positive Chvostek and Trousseau signs.
p: Citrate in stored blood chelates calcium, causing hypocalcemia after massive transfusion; treat with IV calcium.

bw: Sudden dizziness, leaning to one side
Crossed sensory loss on face and body
w: Anterior spinal cord injury spares the face and causes bilateral motor loss.
Thalamic lesions cause contralateral hemisensory loss including the face.
p: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome from PICA occlusion: ipsilateral facial pain/temperature loss, contralateral body loss, ataxia, Horner and dysphagia.

bw: Prior small cell lung cancer therapy
w: Tobacco smoking is a risk factor but the 2-year latency after alkylating agents points to chemotherapy.
A vegan diet causes B12 deficiency with megaloblastic changes.
p: Therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome follows alkylating agents (5-7 years) or topoisomerase inhibitors (1-3 years).

w: Hospitalization is for imminent danger, which is not described.
Family therapy helps but does not reduce immediate lethal means.
p: Means restriction (removing firearms) is a key suicide prevention step in depressed adolescents; follow with close monitoring.

w: Ceftriaxone is ineffective because Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall.
Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam and does not work against organisms without a cell wall.
p: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (cholesterol-containing membrane, no cell wall, cold agglutinins) responds to macrolides, doxycycline or fluoroquinolones.

w: Pancreatic insufficiency has a normal d-xylose test.
Bacterial overgrowth would improve with rifaximin and normalize d-xylose.
p: Abnormal d-xylose indicates mucosal malabsorption; celiac disease causes villous atrophy, with anti-tTG antibodies and response to a gluten-free diet.

bw: Radial wrist pain holding an infant
Pain with ulnar deviation of fist
w: Carpal tunnel syndrome causes median nerve paresthesias, not radial wrist pain over the tendons.
Mallet finger is a distal phalanx extensor tendon avulsion.
p: De Quervain tenosynovitis (abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis) is positive on Finkelstein test; treat with thumb spica splint and NSAIDs.
